paraphrased_fact: BWSSB reports managing nearly 16,000 public borewells across Bengaluru, with 1,800 borewells currently fitted with IoT telemetry devices and plans to equip an additional 6,000 borewells by March 2027.
source_citation: NIE Bengaluru Report (30 Sep 2026), Quotes from BWSSB Chairperson, Paras 2-3
conflict_details: Disagrees with JICA Feb 2026 survey which reported 3,000 monitored pilot wells. The September 2026 Chairperson statement specifies 1,800 active units with 6,000 more planned.

paraphrased_fact: JICA digital architecture survey records an online well monitoring initiative covering 3,000 wells with online on/off control, water volume, and energy monitoring.
source_citation: JICA Data Collection Survey on Enhancement of DX Utilization (Feb 2026), Table 2-31, p. 42
conflict_details: Disagrees with BWSSB Chairperson statement (1,800 active / 6,000 planned). Retained as documented survey figure.

paraphrased_fact: Borewell IoT devices transmit groundwater depth, extracted water quantity, and pump operational hours to a centralized dashboard in real time to prevent dry running and motor burnout.
Treated drinking water is lifted approximately 450 meters from the Cauvery River basin over 100 kilometers through three massive intermediate booster stages at TK Halli, Harohalli, and Tataguni.
source_citation: Yokogawa Electric Corporation, BWSSB Success Story (2015), p. 1

paraphrased_fact: Centralized SCADA monitors pumping station discharge pressure, total electrical power consumption, individual pump volumetric discharge, and pump operational run/trip status.
source_citation: Yokogawa Electric Corporation (2015), 'Data collected from each water related facility', p. 2

paraphrased_fact: BWSSB initiated deployment of AI-based predictive energy and vibration diagnostics across Cauvery Stage IV pump houses to detect impeller cavitation and reduce peak power tariffs.
source_citation: NIE Bengaluru Report (15 Jan 2026), 'BWSSB turns to AI to cut power costs at pump houses'

paraphrased_fact: T.K. Halli is the centralized water treatment headworks treating raw water from Cauvery Stages I through IV with a cumulative operating capacity of 1,475 MLD (Stage I: 540 MLD, Stage II: 300 MLD, Stage III: 300 MLD, Stage IV: 335 MLD). Stage V expansion adds 775 MLD.
source_citation: JICA Phase 3 Final Report Part 4 (p. 17-9) and Yokogawa 2015 Case Study (p. 1)

paraphrased_fact: Yokogawa supervisory system instruments WTP raw-water inflow rate, raw-water turbidity, treated-water quantity, residual chlorine, treated-water turbidity, and substation power consumption.
source_citation: Yokogawa Electric Corporation (2015), Section: 'Examples of data collected', p. 2

paraphrased_fact: Centralized telemetry at major STPs (Vrishabhavathi Valley, K&C Valley, Hebbal) records treated effluent pH, Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD), Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), Total Suspended Solids (TSS), Dissolved Oxygen (DO), effluent color, temperature, ammonium, and total nitrogen.
source_citation: Yokogawa Electric Corporation (2015), Sewage Treatment Plant telemetry register, p. 2

paraphrased_fact: Major ground level service reservoirs (High Grounds, Mount Joy, Central Jail Facility, Machilibetta) are continuously monitored for water level, instantaneous inflow process flow rate, and cumulative volume.
source_citation: Yokogawa Electric Corporation (2015), GLR Supervisory Specifications, p. 2

paraphrased_fact: CAG Audit Report No. 3 of 2022 documented 11,646.04 km of water supply lines and 9,989.53 km of underground sewerage lines. However, the audit revealed 84,916 inconsistent GIS entries out of 202,788 records, missing pipe depth/pressure attributes, and road shapefile datum shifts.
source_citation: Comptroller & Auditor General of India, Karnataka Compliance Audit 2022, Paras 2.2.7.1-2.2.7.3, pp. 35-36

paraphrased_fact: JICA survey documents 1,500 bulk electromagnetic flow meters installed across District Metered Areas (DMAs) transmitting real-time inflow and outflow to calculate physical distribution losses.
BWSSB centralized SCADA architecture ingests over 500 remote DMA data points via OPC standards from third-party RTUs into a centralized Fast/Tools SCADA server at Cauvery Bhavan.
source_citation: Yokogawa Electric Corporation (2015), System Integration Architecture, p. 2
